chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Hasan ibn Atiyya, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The Angel Gabriel (peace be upon him) hardly came to me except that he would say: O Muhammad! Guard against the enmity of men and their hostility.'
ai.seo_question: What did the Angel Gabriel advise the Prophet to guard against regarding people?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith highlights the divine urgency of Gabriel’s repeated counsel to the Prophet, underscoring that interpersonal animosity is a critical spiritual threat. In Shia scholarship, this is often interpreted as a warning against the subtle erosion of unity through personal grudges, linking social harmony directly to spiritual purity. The emphasis on 'shahnā’' (ill-will) suggests that even latent hostility can escalate into open enmity, necessitating proactive reconciliation.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Hassan Bin Atiyya, from Umar Bin Yazeed, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Almost every time Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> came to me<sup>saww</sup>, said: ‘O Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>! Fear disputing the men and their animosity’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from al- Hassan ibn ‘Atiyyah from ‘Umar ibn Yazid from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Almost every time Jibril (Gabriel), on coming to me, would say, “O Muhammad, guard (your) anger against men and animosity to them. ’” (This Hadith is a repeat of H 5 perhaps by the scribe)
